facts.text: Bottom line up front (BLUF) is a writing rule that puts the conclusion and requested decision first; a one-page summary applies that rule so an executive can grasp the decision, confidence and risks in a page or two.
facts.quote: Bottom line up front (BLUF) is the writing rule that the conclusion and the decision requested come first

facts.text: BLUF is a military writing rule from United States Army Regulation 25-50 that presents the answer before the explanation.
facts.quote: BLUF, a military rule from United States Army Regulation 25-50, reverses that: say the answer, then explain.

facts.text: Minto's Pyramid Principle is a consulting counterpart to BLUF, using a situation-complication-question-answer opening.
facts.quote: Minto's Pyramid Principle, with its situation-complication-question-answer opening, is the consulting version of the same idea

facts.text: The booklet's one-to-two-page executive decision brief addresses, in order: the requested decision; why now; what will and will not exist by the deadline; confidence, including P50 and P80 dates and deadline probability; top risks; stop conditions; fallback; and leadership resources and decisions needed.
facts.quote: the probability or confidence (P50 and P80 dates and the probability of meeting the deadline); the top risks; what "stop" looks like; the fallback; and the resources and decisions needed from leadership.

facts.text: Engineers and safety specialists need a technical view of the executive brief's underlying truth that includes the chain of reasoning, model credibility, assumptions, coverage, acceptance thresholds and open disputes.
facts.quote: Engineers and safety specialists then need a different view of the same truth: the chain of reasoning, model credibility, assumptions, coverage, acceptance thresholds and open disputes

facts.text: The gate card is another recurring one-page instrument in the booklet.
facts.quote: Three other one-page instruments recur: the gate card;

facts.text: The booklet's one-page evidence ledger records the claim, evidence required, method, acceptance criterion, owner, due date, status and limitation.
facts.quote: the evidence ledger (claim, evidence required, method, acceptance criterion, owner, due date, status, limitation)

facts.text: The one-page credibility map from Chapter 13 shows every safety claim, whether supporting evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, the real data validating the underlying model, remaining uncertainty and who may accept the claim.
facts.quote: a credibility map showing every safety claim, whether its evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, what real data validated the model behind it, the uncertainty remaining and who may accept it.

facts.text: No controlled study shows that BLUF, a six-page narrative or a pyramid structure increases the likelihood of technical-program approval; the booklet classifies these presentation formats as popular and unproven.
facts.quote: No controlled study shows that BLUF, a six-page narrative or a pyramid structure makes a technical program more likely to be approved; the booklet classes them as popular and unproven.

facts.text: A survey of 1,048 business decisions found that decision process explained more variance in outcomes than analysis quality.
facts.quote: One survey of 1,048 business decisions found that the decision process explained more of the variance in outcomes than the quality of the analysis

facts.text: Reviewers are won by closing weaknesses rather than adding upside, so the first page of the program brief should plainly state the hardest uncertainty and fallback instead of leading with promised savings.
facts.quote: Reviewers are won by closing weaknesses, not by adding upside, so the first page should state the hardest uncertainty and the fallback plainly rather than lead with promised savings
